findings.summary: If time_ms is intended as event/physical time and omission pulses are online prediction errors, allowing a future-dated row already present in the same API batch to alter whether an earlier omission is emitted is an ordinary non-anticipation/causality violation or explicit look-ahead privilege, not a novel cognitive mechanism.
sources: Classical causal/non-anticipative systems semantics: output at time t depends only on present/past inputs

findings.summary: Dataflow/event-time models and discrete-event simulation separate modeled event time from processing/batching time and use explicit event-time progress/chronological scheduling. This supplies a mature ordinary reference for the EVENT_TIME_CAUSAL arm and for partition-invariance requirements.
sources: Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model, PVLDB 8(12), 2015, DOI 10.14778/2824032.2824076
Winter Simulation Conference literature on DES chronology and causal ordering

findings.summary: Kahn-style deterministic stream models establish the broader principle that transport/scheduling choices need not alter logical outputs. For SparkBrain, if API chunking is not a modeled input, legal repartitioning of the same timestamped stream should be a metamorphic invariance property.
sources: Gonnord et al., A Survey on Parallelism and Determinism, ACM Computing Surveys 55(10), 2023, DOI 10.1145/3564529
Gilles Kahn, The Semantics of a Simple Language for Parallel Programming, 1974

findings.summary: Current omission-response neuroscience treats omission activity as tied to the expected time of a missing event and distinguishes ordinary local regularity mechanisms from richer model-based prediction. This makes event-time deadline adjudication scientifically meaningful while providing no novelty rescue for the batching effect.
sources: Yaron et al., Nothing Really Matters: What Omission Responses Reveal About the Predictive Brain, European Journal of Neuroscience 63(10), 2026, DOI 10.1111/ejn.70566

novelty_or_reduction_impact: STRONG_ORDINARY_ARCHITECTURE_REDUCTION: the observed batching sensitivity is naturally explained by non-anticipation, event-time progress and deterministic stream-semantics failures. Future-dated rows in one host-language batch can update expectation state before an earlier omission deadline is adjudicated. The completed Architecture artifact therefore supports an API/reproducibility issue, not a new cognitive principle.
